subject: Dedicated capacity preflight: traffic shape and session inventory for DriftLabs
messages:
From: Ari Shah <ari@driftlabs.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood Dedicated evaluation — traffic snapshot and initial questions

Hi Rafael / Marissa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier this week. We're excited to move from proof-of-concept to a reserved fleet discussion. Attached is a first-pass traffic snapshot (driftlabs_token_profile.csv) and a small sample of session traces (session_samples.jsonl). High-level notes: 

- Peak burst: ~140 concurrent sessions during product launch spikes (approx 09:00-10:30 PST).
- Sustained baseline: ~18 concurrent sessions during weekdays.
- Typical prompt mix: search-style queries (short prompts, 15–40 tokens) ~55% of requests; conversational assistants (multi-turn) ~30% (prompts 60–220 tokens; responses ~80–450 tokens); long-form generation for summaries ~15% (prompts 300–1200 tokens, responses ~500–2500 tokens).
- Expected QPS: baseline 2.5 qps, burst 20–24 qps (5–10 minute spikes).
- Desired p99 token latency: <= 150ms for short prompts; for long-form we care more about throughput than tight p99.

Questions for sizing:
1) How do you recommend mapping the multi-modal prompt mix above to GPU SKUs?
2) Are there autoscale/burst approaches in Dedicated that allow short 10–15 minute capacity uplift without full overcommit?
3) Does Redwood provide guidance for KV-cache sizing given multi-turn sessions?

Timeline: procurement kicks off mid-August; we'd like a draft Dedicated sizing + cost delta by Aug 2 so we can include it in our procurement packet.

Thanks — attaching the two files for your review.

Best,
Ari Shah
Head of Platform
DriftLabs

Attachments: driftlabs_token_profile.csv (CSV, 42 KB); session_samples.jsonl (JSONL, 85 KB)

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Ari Shah <ari@driftlabs.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Jul 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood Dedicated evaluation — traffic snapshot and initial questions

Hi Ari — thanks for the files, very helpful. Quick clarifying questions so we scope the Dedicated proposal correctly: 

1) When you report 'concurrent sessions' do you mean active GPU-resident sessions (i.e., KV cache kept warm) or concurrent user connections where many share a pooled session? If the latter, what's the average session lifetime (in seconds)?
2) For multi-turn sessions, what's your median and 95th percentile number of turns per session?
3) Do you expect synchronous blocking calls (user waits until generation completes) or asynchronous/queued background jobs for the long-form summary workload?
4) Any regulatory constraints — e.g., data residency for PII — that would require Private rather than Dedicated?

I'll attach our pre-flight template (redwood_preflight_template.xlsx) — if you can fill the marked cells for token counts by route and sample percentiles for session durations that will let us map to GPU footprints more accurately.

We can support short bursts via configured burst pools (reserved headroom + ephemeral cloud-backed nodes) — I'll include an example configuration in the draft. KV-cache sizing will depend on your average sequence length and per-session turn count; we'll model that after you send the median/95p turns and session duration.

Proposed next step: can you send the populated template by Jul 27? That gives us 3 business days to run a sizing + cost delta for your procurement timeline.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Senior Solutions Engineer — Dedicated
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_preflight_template.xlsx (Excel, 24 KB)

From: Ari Shah <ari@driftlabs.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Jul 2028 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood Dedicated evaluation — traffic snapshot and initial questions

Rafael — thanks for the quick reply. Filled the template and a few notes inline (see attached). Highlights from the updated template and session_samples.jsonl: 

- 'Concurrent sessions' = GPU-resident session objects (we pin KV cache per active session). Average session lifetime: 220s; 95th percentile: 980s.
- Median turns per session: 3; 95th percentile: 12.
- Short prompts (search) are synchronous (user sees result sub-second). Long-form summaries are queued and handled by async workers (no hard p99 SLA).
- We have an internal requirement to keep PII in US regions; Dedicated in us-west is fine.

Burst profile: typical burst arrives as a rapid ramp (30s) to peak and decays over ~8–12 minutes. Launch day simulations show 11k tokens/sec sustained for a 6-minute window with spikes up to 15k tokens/sec for 20–30 seconds.

Procurement: vendor evaluation docs due Aug 8. We'll accept a draft sizing + cost sheet by Aug 2 as discussed.

Thanks,
Ari

Attachments: redwood_preflight_template_filled.xlsx (Excel, 29 KB); session_samples.jsonl (updated)

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 Jul 2028 15:46:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated capacity preflight: traffic shape and session inventory for DriftLabs

Marissa / Ben — forwarding Ari's filled template and session samples (quoted below). Can you run a Dedicated sizing estimate with two scenarios:

A) Conservative: 20% headroom over the 11k tokens/sec 6-minute launch window (assume p95 prompt lengths) mapped to current GPU SKUs (A100-80GB equivalent + quantized 8-bit variants). Include monthly cost delta vs. hosted at current consumption.
B) Cost-optimized: use 2:1 oversubscription for baseline non-burst workload and a compact burst pool (ephemeral cloud-backed nodes) sized to absorb 75% of the 15k tokens/sec short spikes. Call out KV-cache memory assumptions and ETA for canary rollout (2-week canary -> 2-week ramp).

Timing: need initial numbers by EOD Aug 1 local so we can iterate before Ari's procurement review. 

Internal notes: watch for long-form async worker throughput (500–2,500 tokens per response) — this will drive sustained GPU-hours but not p99. For sizing, assume 32-bit float tokens for kernel selection but also produce guidance for int8 quantized variants (performance and cost deltas).

Thanks — Rafael
